newsitem.title: GERMANY: No decision on taxing utility reserves - Bavaria.
newsitem.headline: No decision on taxing utility reserves - Bavaria.

text.p: The finance ministry of the German state of Bavaria said on Friday that no decision had been made on introducing new taxes on the hidden reserves of German utility companies.

The ministry denied newspaper reports which said that utilities would have to pay billions of marks in tax on around 45 billion marks in reserves. The reserves were held to pay for scrapping nuclear plants.

A spokesman for the Bavarian ministry said a meeting of finance ministers from individual German states had rejected a proposal for the introduction of the tax on a federal basis, which meant each individual state has to decide for itself.

The Bonn government said it believed the reserves were justified, but that utilities should be required to pay tax on interest gains, which could amount to around 750 million marks a year in tax revenue.
Eight states were against the proposal at the finance ministers meeting, four abstained and four were in favour of the proposed tax.
Sources said that the possibility of the states coming to some kind of out-of-court agreement on the issue had not been ruled out.
German utility companies said previously that they would fight the taxes if they were introduced and said they thought the legislation as it currently stood was correct.
